segments.t: In the quiet backstage hallway, Sofia tells Gabriel that she wants to give up, but Gabriel insists that she quit her desk job at ASK to focus entirely on acting. When a fan and Charlotte Gainsbourg both ask for her autograph on their casts, Sofia realizes she is truly an actress. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Il est temps que j'arrête tout.
Tu as raison d'arrêter l'accueil.
Comment je paye mon loyer maintenant?
Tu joues, c'est ton métier désormais.
J'ai raté ma dernière audition importante.
Tu dois avoir confiance en ton talent.
Excusez-moi, pourriez-vous baisser la voix?
Bonsoir mademoiselle Charlotte Gainsbourg.
La cérémonie était beaucoup trop longue.
Vous avez un plâtre à la jambe?
Vous avez un stylo pour signer?
Vous voulez vraiment ma signature ici?
C'est super, merci beaucoup et bravo!
Tu vois, le public t'admire déjà.
Let's break down the dialogue line by line.
Il est temps que j'arrête tout.
'It is time that I stop everything.' Sofia sighs deeply in the backstage hallway. The subjunctive clause expresses her sudden decision.
Tu as raison d'arrêter l'accueil.
'You are right to stop the front desk.' Gabriel clarifies his meaning at once. The preposition de with infinitive focuses on the desk job.
Comment je paye mon loyer maintenant?
'How do I pay my rent now?' Sofia asks anxiously about her daily finances. The interrogative adverb introduces her practical worry.
Tu joues, c'est ton métier désormais.
'You act, it is your job from now on.' Gabriel insists on her real vocation. The decisive adverb marks a major career shift.
J'ai raté ma dernière audition importante.
'I blew my last important audition.' Sofia laments her missed chance for the film. The compound past recalls the difficult trial.
Tu dois avoir confiance en ton talent.
'You must have confidence in your talent.' Gabriel counters her persistent doubts. The modal verb construction urges self-assurance.
Excusez-moi, pourriez-vous baisser la voix?
'Excuse me, could you lower your voices?' Charlotte Gainsbourg steps out on crutches. The polite conditional softens her gentle request.
Bonsoir mademoiselle Charlotte Gainsbourg.
'Good evening Miss Charlotte Gainsbourg.' Gabriel greets her with deference. The formal title honors the distinguished guest star.
La cérémonie était beaucoup trop longue.
'The ceremony was much too long.' Charlotte shares her weariness with the gala. The comparative adverb highlights the exhausting pace.
Vous avez un plâtre à la jambe?
'You have a cast on your leg?' Sofia looks down with genuine sympathy. The prepositional phrase describes the bulky medical cast.
Vous avez un stylo pour signer?
'Do you have a pen to sign?' Charlotte asks with a conspiratorial smile. The preposition pour with infinitive states her purpose.
Vous voulez vraiment ma signature ici?
'You really want my signature here?' Sofia asks in disbelieving wonder. The adverb expresses her delightful surprise.
C'est super, merci beaucoup et bravo!
'It is great, thank you very much and congratulations!' Charlotte signs off with charm. The enthusiastic interjections praise Sofia warmly.
Tu vois, le public t'admire déjà.

'You see, the public already admires you.' Gabriel smiles proudly at his client. The direct object pronoun emphasizes public respect. Now, listen to the complete dialogue again at normal conversational pace.
